verdicts.bookBottomEdge: REFUTES audit:150. Reference book bottom lands at y=496 (89+407); ours at y=497 (92+405). The audit claimed the reference finishes near y=498 while ours begins lower. Vertical placement is at parity within 3px.

Both sides overlap the book's vertical span in bounding-box terms because the left rail runs alongside the book; that is the reference's own composition, not a clean-room fault.
verdicts.width: OPEN — see the standingSilhouetteRegression block. Our measured width is 31px narrow, but the same measurement collapsed on desktop between the pre-retune and post-retune builds, so this number is contaminated and is not yet evidence of a pose error.

standingSilhouetteRegression.finding: The section 6 retune shrank the measured standing-route silhouette. The previous session scored only the rest case and never re-ran the parity harness, so this was not visible to it.

desktopFirstRestBook.note: Unchanged. The collapse is specific to the standing route, where the cover faces the camera, and does not appear on the rest case, which is ~85% spine.

geometryIsUnchanged.note: Identical to the figure the previous session recorded at scene-contract.md:1387, and projected bounds are pure geometry. The pose did not move; the shading at the silhouette edge did.

reproducibility.note: Width and height in px, then pixel count. The harness is noisy at +/-22px on width because the reference-side idle pause makes route capture a race, and one run in six returned book: null. The retune gap is several times that noise on width and roughly 40% on pixel count, so the regression is not capture variance. The pre-retune figures are a fresh rebuild-and-measure on today's server, not a re-read of the 2026-08-07 file, and they reproduce it exactly.

bisect.method: Single-lever reverts against the committed retune, each with the full build pair (package build:site, then the root Astro build) and three measurement runs.

results.config: A — cover crown set to 0, retuned diffuse kept
B — cover crown kept at 0.12x, baseDiffuseStrength reverted

bisect.conclusion: Neither lever owns the regression alone. The cover crown owns most of the width loss (A recovers 375 -> 424 of a 449 baseline); both levers recover pixel count only to ~149k against a 224k baseline, so they interact. The mask is losing both its outer edge and interior area.
bisect.cause: The retune was authored and scored entirely against desktop.firstRestBook, which the previous session established is ~85% spine. Its cover-side consequences were never measured. The cover carries 12% of a crown whose shape was derived for a round spine, and an overlay contrast authored to raise spine weave. On the standing route the cover is the dominant surface, so both land at full strength on a surface neither was tuned for.
